claims.text: The identity of X in CrFeCoNiX governs whether a coherent, slow-growing protective oxide forms above 900 °C.
CrFeCoNiAl promotes formation of an Al-rich, high-configurational-entropy oxide.
The proposed Al-rich oxide bonds strongly to the CrFeCoNiAl substrate.
The proposed Al-rich oxide significantly retards oxygen diffusion.
Oxides formed on the Si- and Mn-containing variants are less cohesive than those formed on the Al-containing variant.
Oxides formed on CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiMn are more prone to cracking or spallation.
CrFeCoNiX alloys can be examined in controlled single-phase or well-characterized multiphase metallic solid-solution states.
Exposure at or above 900 °C in an oxidative or corrosive atmosphere produces an oxide scale at the substrate–oxide interface.
High configurational disorder in the Al-rich oxide leads to a dense and adherent scale.
A dense, adherent Al-rich scale impedes oxygen transport and thereby slows oxide growth.
The Al-rich scale minimizes thermal-stress-induced cracking.
The Si- and Mn-containing variants form oxide scales with inferior adhesion and faster growth kinetics.
Under identical exposure conditions, CrFeCoNiAl will have a thinner and slower-growing oxide scale than CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiMn.
The oxide on CrFeCoNiAl will be more homogeneous and crack-free than the oxides on the Si- and Mn-containing variants.
CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiMn will develop thicker, less coherent oxides with more cracking or spallation than CrFeCoNiAl.
Varying only X among Al, Si, and Mn while holding processing, initial state, temperature, atmosphere, and exposure duration constant provides the controlled comparison.
The proposed comparison is conducted at 950 °C for 100 hours in a controlled oxidizing atmosphere.
Failure of the Al-containing alloy to produce a significantly thinner, more coherent, and more adherent scale than both comparator alloys would falsify the hypothesis.
An absence of clear differences in oxygen diffusion rate and oxide stability among the variants would falsify the hypothesis.
